mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or if Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5%, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances when GDPC1 declines for 2 consecutive quarters, or if Rank IC < 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances when INDPRO increases > 1%, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth exceeds 2% in a quarter and housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in the same period, it signals robust economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 2% and HOUST increase > 5% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 2% and HOUST increase > 5%, or if Rank IC < 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS increases > 300,000, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over two consecutive months signals disinflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL declines for 2 consecutive months, or if Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When retail and food services sales (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same period, it signals strong consumer demand and labor market improvement, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances when RSAFS increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.2%, or if Rank IC < 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.
